security_audit.summary: Two external command findings are confirmed because SKILL.md includes runnable shell examples, including local script execution and deployment commands. The network reconnaissance detections and most backtick detections are false positives from generic prose, Markdown file references, or code fences. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Runnable command examples may be executed against a user environment.
remediation.suggestion: State that every command requires explicit user approval, especially deployment commands such as kubectl and Helm.

remediation.issue: The deployment-oriented quick start example is not clearly separated from safe read-only workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Move deployment commands to a clearly labeled advanced section and provide a dry-run or preview-first workflow.

content.value_statement: Teams need prompts that are reliable, measurable, and safe in production. This skill guides prompt design, evaluation, RAG tuning, and agent architecture for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains prompt engineering patterns for production LLM workflows.
Provides reference guidance for LLM evaluation and RAG evaluation.
Covers agentic system design, observability, reliability, and security topics.
Lists production targets for latency, throughput, availability, and error rates.
Includes example CLI wrappers for prompt optimization, RAG evaluation, and agent orchestration.
limitations: The included Python scripts are lightweight wrappers and do not implement full optimization logic.
It does not connect to model providers or evaluation platforms by itself.
Some command examples require project files, tests, or infrastructure that may not exist.
It does not replace a security review for prompts, datasets, or deployment workflows.

use_cases.title: Design a Reliable Prompt Workflow
use_cases.description: Create reusable prompts with clear inputs, outputs, checks, and evaluation criteria.

use_cases.title: Plan LLM Evaluation Coverage
use_cases.description: Define quality, safety, latency, and regression checks before releasing an AI feature.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Assess agent workflows for observability, reliability, resource use, and deployment readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt for clarity, missing context, and output structure. Suggest a revised version and explain each change briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Evaluation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an evaluation plan for this LLM workflow. Include success criteria, failure modes, sample test cases, and release gates.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a RAG Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this RAG workflow. Recommend improvements for retrieval quality, grounding, citation behavior, latency, and regression testing.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Agent System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production agent workflow for this task. Cover tools, state, safety controls, observability, evaluation, rollback, and cost controls.

output_examples.input: A support team wants a prompt that gives consistent refund policy answers.
output: Clarify the policy source and required customer context.
Add a structured answer format with policy citation and next action.
Test edge cases for expired orders, missing receipts, and regional rules.

output_examples.input: A product team needs an evaluation plan for a document question answering feature.
output: Measure answer accuracy, citation coverage, refusal quality, and latency.
Use representative documents and adversarial queries in every release check.
Block release when unsupported answers exceed the agreed threshold.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead wants to assess an agent that updates project tasks.
output: Separate read-only planning from actions that change state.
Require confirmation before writes, assignments, or status changes.
Log tool calls, user approvals, failures, and rollback steps.

best_practices: Define task inputs, allowed tools, output format, and evaluation criteria before optimizing wording.
Use small test sets with expected behavior before expanding to larger automated evaluations.
Separate read-only analysis from actions that change files, systems, or customer data.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague role prompts without task context, constraints, or success criteria.
Do not treat one good model response as proof that a prompt is production ready.
Do not let agents run deployment or mutation commands without explicit user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design prompts, evaluation plans, RAG workflows, and agent systems for production LLM applications.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it run LLM evaluations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and lightweight script wrappers, but full evaluation logic must be implemented by the user.

faq.question: Can it improve existing prompts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review prompts for clarity, context, output structure, safety checks, and measurable success criteria.

faq.question: Is it suitable for agent design?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for tools, state, reliability, observability, safety controls, and deployment readiness.

faq.question: What should users check before running command examples?
faq.answer: Users should review each command, confirm the target environment, and approve any action that changes files or infrastructure.
